title: Tenant profile API, SDK and Terraform behavior

prose.text: Use this when automating tenant profiles or reading them through a tool.

prose.label: Booleans.
prose.text: {{go-omits-false-flags}} {{go-false-not-sent}} The general mechanism is in [[shared.sdk-go.zero-value-writes]]. What the server does with an omitted false is open {{gap:omitted-false-server-reaction}}.

prose.label: Rule references.
prose.text: {{tf-profile-ids-cap-8}} The rule field and its limits: [[zia.tenant-profiles]] and [[zia.tenant-profiles.limits]]. Other provider fidelity traps: [[zia.terraform.field-fidelity]].

checks.do: Whether the provider version predates 4.7.23 when a plan rejects more than eight profiles on one rule, before blaming policy.

endpoint.statement: Tenant profiles are read and written at `/zia/api/v1/tenancyRestrictionProfile` (list, create) and `/tenancyRestrictionProfile/{id}` (get, update by PUT, delete). The Go SDK updates with PUT.

python-method-names.statement: The Python service `client.zia.tenancy_restriction_profile` names its methods `list_restriction_profile`, `get_restriction_profile`, `add_restriction_profile`, `update_restriction_profile`, `delete_restriction_profile` and `list_app_item_count`.

go-functions.statement: The Go SDK package `tenancy_restriction` exposes `Get`, `GetByName` (a case-insensitive name match across all pages), `Create`, `Update`, `Delete`, `GetAll` and `GetAppItemCount`.

item-type-enum.statement: The API accepts eighteen `itemTypePrimary` and `itemTypeSecondary` tokens, a single flat list with no per-application grouping.

tf-tokens-unvalidated.statement: The Terraform resource does not validate `app_type`, `item_type_primary`, `item_type_secondary` or `item_value`: the first three are free strings and `item_value` is a set of free strings, and each description points to the API reference.

quotes: "app_type": { Type: schema.TypeString, Optional: true, Description: `Restricted tenant profile application type. See the Tenancy Restriction Profile API for the list of available application types: https://help.zscaler.com/zia/cloud-app-control-policy#/tenancyRestrictionProfile-get`, },

"item_type_primary": { Type: schema.TypeString, Optional: true, Description: `Tenant profile primary item type. See the Tenancy Restriction Profile API for the list of available items: https://help.zscaler.com/zia/cloud-app-control-policy#/tenancyRestrictionProfile-get`, },

"item_type_secondary": { Type: schema.TypeString, Optional: true, Description: `Tenant profile secondary item type. See the Tenancy Restriction Profile API for the list of available items: https://help.zscaler.com/zia/cloud-app-control-policy#/tenancyRestrictionProfile-get`, },
Type: schema.TypeSet, Optional: true, Elem: &schema.Schema{Type: schema.TypeString}, Description: `Tenant profile item value for YouTube category. See the Tenancy Restriction Profile API

tf-tokens-unvalidated.conditions: Statement changed from "each is a free string": item_value is a TypeSet of strings. The quotes now show each full schema block, none with a ValidateFunc.

app-item-count.statement: A separate call returns how many items of an item type are already in use for an application, with an optional `excludeProfile` profile ID to leave out. The Go SDK sends the optional ID; the Python method does not accept it, although its docstring lists `exclude_profile`.

quotes: exclude_profile (int, optional): Profile ID to exclude from the item count calculation.

go-omits-false-flags.statement: The Go SDK tags all five boolean flags (`restrictPersonalO365Domains`, `allowGoogleConsumers`, `msLoginServicesTrV2`, `allowGoogleVisitors`, `allowGcpCloudStorageRead`) with `omitempty`, and the Terraform resource builds the struct directly from state.

go-false-not-sent.statement: So a flag set to false is not sent, and Terraform or Go cannot write false explicitly.
go-false-not-sent.conditions: Follows from the tags and Go's encoding/json dropping a false field tagged omitempty (the general mechanism claim). Not observed on the wire for this resource.

last-modified-fields.statement: The Go struct carries `lastModifiedTime` and `lastModifiedUserId`, which the Python model lacks; in Terraform the tenant profile data source exposes them as computed attributes.

quotes: The time the tenant was last modified

tf-profile-ids-cap-8.statement: Terraform provider versions before 4.7.23 capped `tenancy_profile_ids` on `zia_cloud_app_control_rule` at eight, below the 16 profiles per rule the limits page documents. 4.7.23 removed the local cap, leaving the limit to the API.

quotes: in the resource `zia_cloud_app_control_rule` to allow API own limit delegation.
Tenant Profiles per Rule | 16 tenant profiles | Each Cloud App Control Policy rule can have up to 16 tenant profiles associated with it.

tf-profile-ids-cap-8.conditions: Version-scoped; a plan against an older provider that rejects more than eight profile IDs is this defect, not policy drift.

no-bare-profile-names.statement: The bare names such as `list_profiles` or `get_profile` do not exist on the Python tenant profile service; calls must use the `*_restriction_profile` names.
no-bare-profile-names.conditions: The client file at the pinned SDK defines only the six methods named in python-method-names besides the constructor; a quote cannot pin the absence of other method names in code.

omitted-false-server-reaction.title: What the service does when a false flag is omitted from a PUT
omitted-false-server-reaction.detail: Because the Go SDK drops a false boolean, a Terraform change from true to false sends no member for the flag. No source says whether the service then keeps the stored value, resets it to the default, or clears it. For Allow Personal Office 365 Domains and the Google options the console defaults make false the default, but a change from true to false is the case to test.
omitted-false-server-reaction.blocks: whether Terraform can turn a tenant-profile flag off
